reasons.reader_question: Two sharp questions: what 'hold every way' means for Neshar, and who gave Raghu's pairs the song.
reasons.change: Ila now leads him, he trusts her bearing, and the name trade turns knowledge into a nightly exchange with consequences.
reasons.romance_movement: The trade is new and costed. Mutual rescue moves them from wary allies to people who have each held the other's life.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Shown through action: he feeds rope an inch at a time, gives the spring unasked, and they share the goat-belay laugh.
reasons.character_logic: Ila the measurer gets her own pace arithmetic and the crag's side wrong. Smart choices otherwise, especially her exact answer.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Her true answer arms his suspicion, and his name hands the crown a campsite. Both costs are named on the page.
reasons.prose: Clean, varied and concrete. Some narrated interpretation, and the belay sound beat echoes chapter 5 almost word for word.
reasons.continuity: Matches F451, F458 to F464, F468, F674 and F237 (Tamar's Shoulder at seven). No conflict with the bible.

fixes: At 'Three hundred of your paces past the stone... Two hundred and seventy of mine', the arithmetic is backwards (Irrational behaviour). Ila said Kunal's paces are two fingers longer, so 300 of his is about 320 of hers, not 270. Either show the subtraction aloud (the hump's length) or change the figure. Make the closing 'Then I was thirty-odd out' match: forty of his paces is about forty-three of hers.

At 'Black rock stood out of the white, a long crag on the left', the geometry conflicts with 'Ninety-four degrees' while walking north-east by north. A crag due east sits on their right. Change 'on the left' to 'on the right, off her shoulder', or have Ila note that the bearing puts the crag behind the line they thought they held. Readers who audit the map will catch this.

At 'It was no gift. It was a man handing the lead', the narration interprets his trust for the reader (Narrated-only chemistry). Cut those three sentences and show the cost instead. For example, Kunal unties the rope from his wrist and reties it round his hip before she asks, or his hands stay out from his sides, empty. Also rework 'a grunt, a boot skidding on ice' so it does not echo chapter 5's belay line.
reader_question: Now that Kunal knows the commission says the crown 'may hold every way', and Raghu walked a line only the song could give, what will each name cost them both?
new_facts_assessment: Raghu's drifted hobnail prints on the bearing are necessary. They raise the stakes under the buried boulder and open the 'who gave them the song' question. They are consistent with F674 (nine heads, heel bar) and F468 (a day or more ahead). Watch one tension: Kunal says Hari 'never gave it to a soul', yet children learn these songs as nonsense. Clarify that he means outsiders.
